purpose: A separate historical reconstruction, distinct from the live, single-reading Human Stupidity Index published in data/hsi.json. It exists so that, over time, readers can look for correlations between this index and other historical phenomena -- it is a research and pattern-spotting artifact, not a claim that every value here is on the same footing as the live index's primary-sourced reading. It must never be merged into or presented as the live reading.
rules_applied: Every non-empty value is traced to a real, fetched, machine-parsed source file -- nothing is invented to fill a gap.

Where an indicator's underlying phenomenon did not exist yet (no ODA before 1960, no Doomsday Clock before 1947, etc.), it is omitted for those years rather than estimated, the same way press_freedom is already dropped from the live pillar average before 2002.
Where a value is modeled/interpolated rather than a directly published annual figure (conflict_deaths 1900-1945), this is flagged explicitly, point by point, not left implicit.

Where the real, original primary file could not be fetched (bot-detection, non-machine-readable PDF, portal-gated download), a traceable secondary republication was used instead and is disclosed as such -- a documented exception to the live index's primary-source-only rule, made only for this historical layer.

co2.data_quality_note: REAL DATA, directly fetched and parsed from the NOAA NCEI text file (law2018co2-noaa.txt), which is a machine-readable tab-delimited format. 43 calendar years with at least one measurement between 1900-1959 (not every year has a sample; ice-core gas-age dating has some smoothing/diffusion in the firn column, so single-year values carry that inherent uncertainty). Splices cleanly onto Mauna Loa instrumental record from 1958/1959 onward (already used as the live source elsewhere in this project). Multiple samples in a year were averaged; CO2err (measurement uncertainty) was not propagated into these averages.

data.unit: V-Dem Liberal Democracy Index, 0 (least) to 1 (most democratic)
data.source_name: V-Dem (Varieties of Democracy) Democracy Report v16 (2026), country-average World aggregate, as processed and republished by Our World in Data
data.note: World = unweighted average across all polities V-Dem covers/imputes for that year (V-Dem's own coverage starts at ~1789 with a small number of polities and expands over time; OWID imputes some non-sovereign territories using their historical parent state's score). Not the raw V-Dem download file itself — this is OWID's ETL-processed CSV, which is the practical machine-readable path since the raw V-Dem .csv/.dta from v-dem.net requires downloading a large multi-hundred-variable file via their institute's own dataset page.

This is V-Dem data at one remove: I did not download the original v-dem.net .csv/.rds/.dta package (that requires navigating the V-Dem Institute's own data portal rather than a single fetchable file), but OWID's republished CSV is explicitly sourced from and citation-traceable to V-Dem, and is annual, not just benchmark years. extreme_poverty.data_quality_note: REAL DATA. Did not extract numbers directly from the original Bourguignon & Morrisson (2002) AER PDF (its tables are not machine-readable via WebFetch — scanned/formatted academic PDF). Instead fetched OWID's digitized/republished CSV (ourworldindata.org/grapher/world-population-in-extreme-poverty-absolute.csv), which OWID's own metadata explicitly attributes to 'Ravallion, Bourguignon and Morrison, and World Bank (2019)'. The benchmark years present (1820, 1850, 1870, 1890, 1910, 1929, 1950) exactly match the benchmark years the task specified as B&M's original years, which is strong circumstantial confirmation this is the real B&M series, not a different one. Poverty threshold in this OWID vintage is $1.90/day at 2011 PPP; note B&M's original paper used $1/day and $2/day at 1985 PPP — OWID states it rescaled/spliced the original estimates onto the modern line, so treat the exact percentage as OWID's harmonized version of B&M, not a verbatim transcription of the 2002 paper's own published percentages. 7 points are genuine B&M benchmark years; the rest (18 points, 1960-2015) are the World Bank-based continuation, included for context.

data.unit: count of wars meeting COW battle-death thresholds (>=1000 total battle deaths, or the applicable COW war-inclusion criterion for that war type) active (ongoing) at any point in that calendar year
data.source_name: Correlates of War Project: Inter-State War Data v4.0, Extra-State War Data v4.0, Intra-State War Data v4.1
data.note: Computed directly from each war's StartYear1/EndYear1 fields; a war counts as 'active' in every calendar year from its start year through its end year inclusive. Does not include Non-State War data (a 4th COW file, also fetched but not used here) or COW's own MID (Militarized Interstate Disputes) dataset, which covers lower-intensity disputes not reaching the war threshold.

active_conflicts.data_quality_note: REAL DATA, directly computed from real downloaded COW CSVs (not fabricated). 108 annual points, 1900-2007 (COW's Intra-State v4.1 file — the update-frequency bottleneck — stops at 2007; Inter-State v4.0 stops ~2003, Extra-State v4.0 stops ~2004; counts for the tail years 2004-2007 therefore only reflect ongoing intra-state wars). No UCDP/PRIO Armed Conflict Dataset splice was attempted for post-2008 continuation (that would be a 4th dataset beyond the 6 the task named).
active_conflicts.published_disclaimer: Sourced via a traceable secondary republication (Our World in Data), not the original primary file, because the primary file was bot-gated, portal-gated, or a non-machine-readable academic PDF. OWID explicitly cites its own upstream source for this series.

data.unit: battle deaths (military + war-related), world total, modeled annual
data.source_name: Correlates of War Project: Inter-State/Extra-State/Intra-State War Data (v4.0/v4.0/v4.1) -- battle-death totals per war, redistributed to annual
data.note: NOT an original annual figure. COW publishes one total battle-death count per war (all sides), not year-by-year. This value = that war's total battle deaths / number of calendar years the war spanned, summed across every war active that year, then rounded. This is a modeling choice (linear/even distribution across the war's duration), not a citable annual estimate on its own -- treat with caution, especially for short spikes.

conflict_deaths.data_quality_note: MIXED CONFIDENCE. Two real, directly-downloaded source files were used but combined at different quality levels: (1) 1900-1945 (46 points) is DERIVED from real COW war-level totals but the annual breakdown is my own even-distribution-across-war-years modeling choice, not a published annual series -- flag this to a human before treating it as equivalent-quality to the rest. (2) 1946-2008 (63 points) is a REAL annual series, directly summed from PRIO's own year-by-year battle-death field, with the caveat that some conflict-years have missing estimates (excluded, so total undercounts). No data was fabricated for either segment; where COW/PRIO didn't have a number, no number is given (years absent from the array had zero known wars/conflicts contributing a usable figure, not an invented zero).
conflict_deaths.published_disclaimer: Values for 1900-1945 are not a published annual series. Correlates of War reports one battle-death total per war; each war's total was spread evenly across the calendar years it lasted to produce an annual figure. This is a modeling choice made for this project, not a citation of an existing annual estimate. From 1946 onward, values are a real annual series (PRIO Battle Deaths Dataset).

data.unit: world military expenditure as % of world GDP (CONSTRUCTED, units not fully matched -- see note)
data.source_name: Numerator: Correlates of War National Material Capabilities v7.0 ('milex', thousands of current-year US dollars), summed across all COW system-member states. Denominator: 'Global GDP over the long run' (Maddison Database 2010 / Maddison Project Database 2023 / World Bank), as processed by Our World in Data, in constant international-$ (2021 prices).
data.note: CAUTION: numerator (COW milex) is NOMINAL, current-year exchange-rate-converted US dollars; denominator (OWID/Maddison GDP) is REAL, PPP-adjusted, constant-2021-international-dollars. These are not on the same price/currency basis, so this ratio is NOT equivalent to the standard 'military expenditure (% of GDP)' metric (e.g. SIPRI, World Bank), which compares both figures in the SAME year's SAME currency terms. Sanity check: this construction gives ~1.0-1.4% for 1990-2016, versus SIPRI's real published figure of roughly 2.2-2.6% for the same years -- confirming the mismatch understates the true ratio, likely by something like a third to a half, and more unpredictably in earlier, poorer, less-monetized years. World milex summed across 35 COW system-member states with non-missing data that year -- COW's system membership list itself is narrower than 'the whole world' in the earliest decades.

mil_gdp.data_quality_note: LOW-MEDIUM CONFIDENCE, EXPLICITLY CONSTRUCTED (as the task anticipated -- 'no ready-made single series exists'). Both inputs are real, directly downloaded, machine-readable files: COW National Material Capabilities v7.0 (NMCv7.zip -> NMC-70-abridged.csv, real annual 'milex' by country 1816-2022) and OWID's Maddison-based 'Global GDP over the long run' (real, annual from 1990, decadal-ish benchmark years before that: 1900,1920,1940,1950,1960,1970,1980,1990). I did NOT fabricate any of the underlying milex or GDP numbers. What IS a methodological construction, and should be treated with real skepticism before shipping: dividing a nominal-exchange-rate military-spending aggregate by a PPP-adjusted constant-price GDP aggregate produces a ratio that is directionally informative (it does track known militarization spikes: WWI, WWII, Cold War buildup) but is NOT numerically equivalent to standard 'military spending as % of GDP' series, and I verified this by comparing against the well-known SIPRI/World Bank modern-era benchmark (real: ~2.2-2.6%; this construction: ~1.0-1.4%). A human should either find a same-basis GDP series (e.g. COW-era nominal world GDP, or a milex series deflated/PPP-converted the same way as the GDP denominator) before using this for anything beyond a rough historical shape, or clearly label the chart as an OWID-Maddison/COW-NMC composite with a unit caveat.
mil_gdp.published_disclaimer: This ratio is constructed for the purpose of seeing the historical shape of military spending relative to the world economy, so it can later be correlated against other phenomena in this reconstruction -- it is not on the same numerical basis as the live index's SIPRI-sourced military-expenditure-as-percent-of-GDP figure and should not be read as directly comparable to it. Verified understatement: this construction yields roughly 1.0-1.4% for 1990-2016, where SIPRI's own modern series shows roughly 2.2-2.6% for the same years, because the two use different price/exchange-rate bases.

temp_anomaly.data_quality_note: NOT RE-RESEARCHED per instructions -- this is the live index's own source (NASA GISTEMP v4, data.giss.nasa.gov/gistemp/tabledata_v4/GLB.Ts+dSST.csv) and it already covers 1880-present, which fully spans the 'back toward 1900' target on its own. No separate historical-extension data file was produced for this indicator; the existing live-data pipeline should just be reused for the historical view as well. BLOCKED: see not_available.temp_anomaly for why this is empty despite the source being real and citable.

not_available.temp_anomaly: Blocked in this pass, not by data availability -- NASA GISTEMP v4 (data.giss.nasa.gov) is reachable and does publish the full annual series 1880-present, but that specific host is unreachable from this build environment's network egress (confirmed: other NASA/NOAA hosts work, this one alone refuses connections). Needs either a retry from an environment that can reach it, or a human-approved alternate mirror.
not_available.doomsday: No real extension exists. The Doomsday Clock concept did not exist before 1947.
not_available.mil_oda: No real extension exists. Official development assistance as a measured concept did not exist before ~1960-61 (OECD DAC founded 1961).
not_available.immunisation: No real extension exists. WHO's Expanded Programme on Immunization began 1974; no global DTP3-equivalent coverage estimate exists before that.
not_available.living_planet: No real extension exists. Scattered species counts exist but were never assembled into a global index before 1970.
not_available.warheads: Not researched in this pass. A real extension to 1945 was identified in an earlier research pass (NRDC/Bulletin Nuclear Weapons Databook, Kristensen & Norris) but the actual annual figures were not fetched.
not_available.press_freedom: Not researched in this pass. A real but non-equivalent proxy (Freedom House 'Freedom of the Press', 1980+, different scale than RSF) was identified in an earlier research pass but not fetched.
not_available.displaced: Not researched in this pass. Only fragmentary, non-global, Europe-centric estimates exist before the 1990s (League of Nations Nansen Office refugee records) -- likely too sparse to include reliably even if fetched.
